336	      color: 0x0c2030, emissive: 0x2a8aa6, emissiveIntensity: 1.4, roughness: 0.3,
337	    })
338	  );
339	  screen.position.set(0, 4.0, 0.82);
340	  screen.rotation.x = -0.28;
341	  g.add(pedestal, screen);
342	  return g;
343	}
344	
345	export function createDroneBayView(renderer, { onExit, onComplete, onNext } = {}) {
346	  const canvas = renderer.domElement;
347	
348	  // ---------- scene & sky ----------
349	  const scene = new THREE.Scene();
350	  scene.background = SKY_CALM.clone();
351	  scene.fog = new THREE.Fog(SKY_CALM.clone(), 90, 320);
352	
353	  const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(
354	    62, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 2000
355	  );
356	
357	  // ---------- lighting ----------
358	  scene.add(new THREE.HemisphereLight(0xcdbcff, 0x3a2f5e, 0.7));
359	  const sun = new THREE.DirectionalLight(SUN_CALM, 1.5);
360	  sun.position.set(60, 90, 40);
361	  scene.add(sun);
362	  scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0x6a5a92, 0.3));
363	
364	  const dome = new THREE.Mesh(
365	    new THREE.SphereGeometry(900, 32, 16),
366	    new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: DOME_CALM.clone(), side: THREE.BackSide, fog: false })
367	  );
368	  scene.add(dome);
369	
370	  // ---------- terrain (the same island) ----------
371	  const terrain = createTerrain({ size: 200, segments: 220, maxHeight: 26, seed: 1337 });
372	  scene.add(terrain.mesh, terrain.water);
373	
374	  const beamTex = makeBeamTexture();
375	
376	  // ---------- the five work sites ----------
377	  const sites = SYSTEMS.map((sys, idx) => {
378	    const anchor = new THREE.Group();
379	    anchor.position.set(sys.pos.x, terrain.heightAt(sys.pos.x, sys.pos.z), sys.pos.z);
380	
381	    const BUILD = {
382	      buildBrokenCoils, buildBrokenNav, buildBrokenDish, buildBrokenVent, buildBrokenStrut,
383	      buildPlasmaRing, buildStarDome, buildGardenPod, buildGravSkid,
384	      buildSignalSpire: () => buildSignalSpire(beamTex),
385	    };
386	    const brokenModel = BUILD[sys.broken]();
387	    const upgradeModel = BUILD[sys.upgrade]();
388	    upgradeModel.visible = false;
389	    anchor.add(brokenModel, upgradeModel);
390	
391	    // Status beam — readable from across the island:
392	    // amber = broken, cyan pulse = drone at work, ice-blue = sealed (review me).
393	    const beam = new THREE.Mesh(
394	      new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.6, 60, 12, 1, true),
395	      new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({
396	        map: beamTex, color: 0xff8a5c, transparent: true, opacity: 0.3,
397	        blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false, side: THREE.DoubleSide,
398	        fog: false,
399	      })
400	    );
401	    beam.position.y = 30;
402	    anchor.add(beam);
403	
404	    // The checkpoint seal: ice + floating trailer id, like Level 1's bank.
405	    const ice = makeIceBlock();
406	    ice.scale.setScalar(1.25);
407	    ice.position.y = 2.6;
408	    ice.visible = false;
409	    anchor.add(ice);
410	    const sprite = makeIdSprite(sys.ckpt);
411	    sprite.position.y = 8.4;
412	    sprite.visible = false;
413	    anchor.add(sprite);
414	
415	    scene.add(anchor);
416	    return {
417	      sys, idx, anchor, brokenModel, upgradeModel, beam, ice, sprite,
418	      state: "broken",      // broken → working → sealed → added
419	      workT: 0,
420	      meltT: 0,             // ice melt animation after ADD TO SHIP
421	    };
422	  });
423	
424	  // ---------- the drone bay: five parked drones by the console ----------
425	  const drones = SYSTEMS.map((_, i) => {
426	    const d = buildDrone();
427	    const x = BAY_ROW.x0 + i * BAY_ROW.dx;
428	    const home = new THREE.Vector3(x, terrain.heightAt(x, BAY_ROW.z) + 1.2, BAY_ROW.z);
429	    d.position.copy(home);
430	    scene.add(d);
431	    return {
432	      model: d, home,
433	      state: "bay",         // bay → flying → working → returning
434	      site: null,
435	      from: new THREE.Vector3(), to: new THREE.Vector3(),
436	      t: 0, dur: 1,
437	      bobOff: Math.random() * 10,
438	    };
439	  });
440	
441	  // Work beam shown under a working drone (one per drone, toggled).
442	  const workBeams = drones.map(() => {
443	    const m = new THREE.Mesh(
444	      new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.25, 1.2, 6, 10, 1, true),
445	      new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({
446	        color: 0x6fe3ff, transparent: true, opacity: 0.5,
447	        blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false, side: THREE.DoubleSide,
448	      })
449	    );
450	    m.visible = false;
451	    scene.add(m);
452	    return m;
453	  });
454	
455	  // ---------- the ship console ----------
456	  const consoleAnchor = new THREE.Group();
457	  consoleAnchor.position.set(
458	    CONSOLE_POS.x, terrain.heightAt(CONSOLE_POS.x, CONSOLE_POS.z), CONSOLE_POS.z
459	  );
460	  consoleAnchor.add(makeConsole());
461	  const consoleGlow = new THREE.PointLight(0xffd27a, 5, 28, 2);
462	  consoleGlow.position.y = 5;
463	  consoleAnchor.add(consoleGlow);
464	  scene.add(consoleAnchor);
465	
466	  // ---------- first-person controller ----------
467	  const fp = createFirstPerson(camera, canvas, {
468	    heightAt: terrain.heightAt,
469	    radius: terrain.radius * 0.96,
470	    eyeHeight: 2.6,
471	    speed: 24,
472	  });
473	  scene.add(fp.controls.object);
474	
475	  // Bird's-eye map (M) — see all five beams at once, keep walking meanwhile.
476	  const overhead = createOverhead(scene, terrain, camera);
477	  function setMap(on) {
478	    if (overhead.on === on) return;
479	    overhead.set(on);
480	    fp.setAlwaysMove(on);                       // arrows work without pointer lock
481	    scene.fog.near = on ? 500 : 90;             // don't fog the map out
482	    scene.fog.far = on ? 1400 : 320;
483	    crosshair?.classList.toggle("hidden", on || !fp.isLocked);
484	  }
485	
486	  // ---------- HUD elements (shared FP set + this level's own) ----------
487	  const promptEl = document.getElementById("fp-prompt");
488	  const controlsEl = document.getElementById("fp-controls");
489	  const crosshair = document.getElementById("crosshair");
490	  const tutorialEl = document.getElementById("tutorial");
491	  const fpShared = document.getElementById("fp-shared");
492	  const termEl = document.getElementById("terminal");
493	  const termHint = document.getElementById("term-hint");
494	  const termInput = document.getElementById("term-input");
495	  const termList = document.getElementById("term-list");
496	  const termMsg = document.getElementById("term-msg");
497	  const termCta = document.getElementById("term-cta");
498	  const dbHud = document.getElementById("db-hud");
499	  const briefingEl = document.getElementById("db-briefing");
500	  const briefingStartBtn = document.getElementById("db-briefing-start");
501	  const countdownEl = document.getElementById("db-countdown");
502	  const countdownTime = document.getElementById("db-countdown-time");
503	  const systemsEl = document.getElementById("db-systems-rows");
504	  const winEl = document.getElementById("db-win");
505	  const winSub = document.getElementById("db-win-sub");
506	  const failEl = document.getElementById("db-fail");
507	
508	  let active = false;
509	  let started = false;
510	  let failed = false;
511	  let reportSent = false;       // `entire dispatch` has been run — the win
512	  let promptText = null;
513	  let controlsLocked = null;
514	  const taught = new Set();
515	  let tutorialTimer = null;
516	  let msgTimer = null;
517	  let winTimer = null;
518	
519	  // Level countdown — the single source of pressure for the whole run.
520	  let timeLeft = TOTAL_TIME;
521	  let timerRunning = false;
522	
523	  // Terminal state. Two modes share the one terminal:
524	  //  "review" — pre-filled `entire checkpoint explain <id>` at a sealed site
525	  //  "report" — type `entire dispatch` (the finish line). Opens in place when
526	  //             the FIFTH system is accepted; reopens at any online system or
527	  //             the bay console if the player wandered off first.
528	  let terminalOpen = false;
529	  let termMode = null;
530	  let reviewSite = null;        // the sealed site being reviewed
531	  let explained = false;        // Enter pressed — the card is showing
532	  let buffer = "";
533	  let dismissedSite = null;     // site the player Esc'd out of (until they leave)
534	  let reportDismissed = false;
535	
536	  const addedCount = () => sites.filter((s) => s.state === "added").length;
537	  const allAdded = () => addedCount() >= sites.length;
538	
539	  // ---------- HUD helpers ----------
540	  function setPrompt(text) {
541	    if (!promptEl || text === promptText) return;
542	    promptText = text;
543	    if (text) { promptEl.textContent = text; promptEl.classList.remove("hidden"); }
544	    else promptEl.classList.add("hidden");
545	  }
546	  function showTutorial(text, ms = 5500) {
547	    if (!tutorialEl) return;
548	    clearTimeout(tutorialTimer);
549	    tutorialEl.textContent = text;
550	    tutorialEl.classList.remove("hidden");
551	    if (ms > 0) tutorialTimer = setTimeout(() => tutorialEl.classList.add("hidden"), ms);
552	  }
553	  function teachOnce(key, text, ms) {
554	    if (taught.has(key)) return;
555	    taught.add(key);
556	    showTutorial(text, ms);
557	  }
558	  function setControls(locked) {
559	    if (!controlsEl) return;
560	    if (locked === controlsLocked && !controlsEl.classList.contains("hidden")) return;
561	    controlsLocked = locked;
562	    controlsEl.innerHTML = `
563	      <span class="control-item">
564	        <span class="control-label">To move</span>
565	        <span class="arrow-keys" aria-label="Arrow keys">
566	          <span class="key key-up">↑</span>
567	          <span class="key key-left">←</span>
568	          <span class="key key-down">↓</span>
569	          <span class="key key-right">→</span>
570	        </span>
571	      </span>
572	      ${locked ? `
573	        <span class="control-item">
574	          <span class="control-label">To look around</span>
575	          <span class="mouse-hint">
576	            <span class="mouse-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>
577	            <span>move mouse</span>
578	          </span>
579	        </span>
580	      ` : ""}
581	      <span class="control-item">
582	        <span class="control-label">Send a subagent</span>
583	        <span class="key">E</span>
584	      </span>
585	      <span class="control-item">
586	        <span class="control-label">Bird's-eye view</span>
587	        <span class="key">M</span>
588	      </span>
589	      <span class="control-item">
590	        <span class="control-label">Return to orbit</span>
591	        <span class="key">B</span>
592	      </span>
593	    `;
594	    controlsEl.classList.remove("hidden");
595	  }
596	  function hideControls() {
597	    controlsLocked = null;
598	    controlsEl?.classList.add("hidden");
599	  }
600	
601	  // ---------- systems status panel ----------
602	  const STATE_LABEL = {
603	    broken: "BROKEN", working: "SUBAGENT AT WORK", sealed: "READY TO REVIEW", added: "ONLINE",
604	  };
605	  function updateSystems() {
606	    if (!systemsEl) return;
607	    systemsEl.innerHTML = sites.map((s) =>
608	      `<div class="db-sys is-${s.state}">` +
609	      `<span class="db-sys-name">${s.sys.name}</span>` +
610	      `<span class="db-sys-state">${STATE_LABEL[s.state]}</span></div>`
611	    ).join("");
612	  }
613	
614	  // ---------- level countdown ----------
615	  function fmtTime(s) {
616	    s = Math.max(0, Math.ceil(s));
617	    return `${Math.floor(s / 60)}:${String(s % 60).padStart(2, "0")}`;
618	  }
619	  function updateClock() {
620	    if (countdownTime) countdownTime.textContent = fmtTime(timeLeft);
621	    countdownEl?.classList.toggle("is-low", timerRunning && timeLeft <= LOW_TIME);
622	    countdownEl?.classList.toggle("is-critical", timerRunning && timeLeft <= CRIT_TIME);
623	  }
624	  function panicFactor() {
625	    if (failed) return 1;
626	    if (!timerRunning || timeLeft > PANIC_TIME) return 0;
627	    let p = (PANIC_TIME - timeLeft) / PANIC_TIME;
628	    p *= p;
629	    if (timeLeft <= CRIT_TIME) {
630	      const throb = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(performance.now() / 85);
631	      p += 0.14 * throb;
632	    }
633	    return Math.min(1, p);
634	  }
635	  function applyPanicSky() {
636	    const p = reportSent ? 0 : panicFactor();
637	    scene.background.copy(SKY_CALM).lerp(SKY_PANIC, p);
638	    scene.fog.color.copy(SKY_CALM).lerp(FOG_PANIC, p);
639	    dome.material.color.copy(DOME_CALM).lerp(DOME_PANIC, p);
640	    sun.color.copy(SUN_CALM).lerp(SUN_PANIC, p * 0.85);
641	  }
642	
643	  // ---------- briefing / win / fail / reset ----------
644	  function showBriefing() {
645	    timerRunning = false;
646	    fp.detach();
647	    tutorialEl?.classList.add("hidden");
648	    briefingEl?.classList.remove("hidden");
649	  }
650	  function startLevel() {
651	    if (started) return;
652	    started = true;
653	    briefingEl?.classList.add("hidden");
654	    fp.attach();
655	    timeLeft = TOTAL_TIME;
656	    timerRunning = true;
657	    updateClock();
658	    showTutorial("Five systems are dark — the amber beams. Walk to one and press E: a subagent takes the job while you move on.", 8500);
659	  }
660	  briefingStartBtn?.addEventListener("click", startLevel);
661	
662	  function failLevel() {
663	    if (failed || reportSent) return;
664	    failed = true;
665	    timerRunning = false;
666	    setMap(false);
667	    closeTerminal(false);
668	    fp.detach();
669	    countdownEl?.classList.remove("is-low", "is-critical");
670	    tutorialEl?.classList.add("hidden");
671	    failEl?.classList.remove("hidden");
672	  }
673	  function resetLevel() {
674	    failed = false;
675	    reportSent = false;
676	    dismissedSite = null;
677	    reportDismissed = false;
678	    clearTimeout(winTimer);
679	    for (const s of sites) {
680	      s.state = "broken";
681	      s.workT = 0; s.meltT = 0;
682	      s.brokenModel.visible = true;
683	      s.upgradeModel.visible = false;
684	      const anim = s.upgradeModel.userData.anim;
685	      if (anim?.type === "spire") anim.beam.visible = false;
686	      s.ice.visible = false;
687	      s.ice.material.opacity = 0.62;
688	      s.sprite.visible = false;
689	    }
690	    for (let i = 0; i < drones.length; i++) {
691	      drones[i].state = "bay";
692	      drones[i].site = null;
693	      drones[i].model.position.copy(drones[i].home);
694	      workBeams[i].visible = false;
695	    }
696	    failEl?.classList.add("hidden");
697	    winEl?.classList.add("hidden");
698	    updateSystems();
699	    timeLeft = TOTAL_TIME;
700	    timerRunning = true;
701	    updateClock();
702	    if (active) fp.attach();
703	    showTutorial("New attempt — the fleet works in parallel. Use all five subagents.", 6000);
704	  }
705	
706	  // ---------- drone dispatching ----------
707	  function assignDrone(site) {
708	    const drone = drones.find((d) => d.state === "bay");
709	    if (!drone) return;                 // shouldn't happen: one drone per system
710	    site.state = "working";
711	    site.workT = 0;
712	    drone.state = "flying";
713	    drone.site = site;
714	    drone.from.copy(drone.model.position);
715	    drone.to.set(site.anchor.position.x, site.anchor.position.y + 6.5, site.anchor.position.z);
716	    drone.t = 0;
717	    drone.dur = Math.max(1, drone.from.distanceTo(drone.to) / DRONE_SPEED);
718	    updateSystems();
719	    teachOnce("assigned",
720	      "The subagent's got it — you're free. Send the others while it works; the clock won't wait.", 7000);
721	  }
722	  function sealSite(site) {
723	    site.state = "sealed";
724	    site.brokenModel.visible = false;
725	    site.upgradeModel.visible = true;   // built — but dormant until ADD TO SHIP
726	    site.ice.visible = true;
727	    site.ice.material.opacity = 0.62;
728	    site.sprite.visible = true;
729	    updateSystems();
730	    teachOnce("sealed",
731	      "A subagent finished while you were away — its work is sealed under a checkpoint. Walk up and see what it actually did.", 8000);
732	  }
733	
734	  // ---------- terminal ----------
735	  function flashTerminal(text, ok) {
736	    if (!termMsg) return;
737	    clearTimeout(msgTimer);
738	    termMsg.textContent = text;
739	    termMsg.classList.remove("show-ok", "show-err");
740	    termMsg.classList.add(ok ? "show-ok" : "show-err");
741	    msgTimer = setTimeout(() => termMsg.classList.remove("show-ok", "show-err"), 3600);
742	  }
743	  function renderTerminal() {
744	    if (!terminalOpen) return;
745	    if (termMode === "review") {
746	      if (!explained) {
747	        // The command comes pre-filled — you never type a checkpoint id.
748	        termHint.textContent = "# what did the subagent actually do? ask the checkpoint";
749	        termInput.textContent = `entire checkpoint explain ${reviewSite.sys.ckpt}`;
750	        termInput.classList.remove("is-dim");
751	        if (termCta) termCta.innerHTML =
752	          `<span class="cta-label">PRESS</span>` +
753	          `<kbd class="cta-key cta-key-yes">Enter</kbd><span class="cta-note">run it</span>`;
754	      } else {
755	        termHint.textContent = "# reviewed — your call";
756	        termInput.textContent = `entire checkpoint explain ${reviewSite.sys.ckpt}`;
757	        termInput.classList.add("is-dim");
758	        if (termCta) termCta.innerHTML =
759	          `<button id="db-add-btn" type="button">ADD TO SHIP</button>` +
760	          `<span class="cta-note">or press <kbd class="cta-key cta-key-yes">Y</kbd></span>`;
761	      }
762	    } else if (termMode === "report") {
763	      termHint.textContent = reportSent
764	        ? "# dispatch sent — the day is on the record"
765	        : "# five jobs accepted — send the day's report";
766	      termInput.textContent = buffer;
767	      termInput.classList.remove("is-dim");
768	      if (termCta) termCta.innerHTML = reportSent ? "" :
769	        `<span class="cta-label">TYPE</span><span class="cta-cmd">entire dispatch</span>`;
770	    }
771	  }
772	  function openTerminal(mode, site) {
773	    if (terminalOpen) return;
774	    terminalOpen = true;
775	    termMode = mode;
776	    reviewSite = site || null;
777	    explained = false;
778	    buffer = "";
779	    fp.detach();
780	    termMsg?.classList.remove("show-ok", "show-err");
781	    termList?.classList.add("hidden");
782	    termEl?.classList.remove("hidden");
783	    renderTerminal();
784	  }
785	  function closeTerminal(dismiss) {
786	    if (!terminalOpen) return;
787	    if (dismiss) {
788	      if (termMode === "review" && reviewSite) dismissedSite = reviewSite;
789	      if (termMode === "report") reportDismissed = true;
790	    }
791	    terminalOpen = false;
792	    termMode = null;
793	    reviewSite = null;
794	    explained = false;
795	    buffer = "";
796	    termEl?.classList.add("hidden");
797	    termList?.classList.add("hidden");
798	    if (active && !failed) fp.attach();
799	  }
800	
801	  // ---------- entire checkpoint explain (pre-filled, Enter to run) ----------
802	  function runExplain() {
803	    if (!reviewSite || explained) return;
804	    explained = true;
805	    const s = reviewSite;
806	    if (termList) {
807	      termList.innerHTML =
808	        `<div class="term-list-row"><span class="tl-key tl-exp-key">checkpoint</span>` +
809	        `<span class="tl-title">${s.sys.ckpt}</span></div>` +
810	        s.sys.card.map(([k, v]) =>
811	          `<div class="term-list-row"><span class="tl-key tl-exp-key">${k}</span>` +
812	          `<span class="tl-title">${v}</span></div>`
813	        ).join("");
814	      termList.classList.remove("hidden");
815	    }
816	    flashTerminal(`explained ${s.sys.ckpt} — ${s.sys.name.toLowerCase()} is now a ${s.sys.became}`, true);
817	    teachOnce("explained",
818	      "That's the story behind the checkpoint — work you didn't watch is never a mystery. If it's good, add it to the ship.", 8000);
819	    renderTerminal();
820	  }
821	
822	  // ---------- ADD TO SHIP ----------
823	  function addToShip() {
824	    if (!reviewSite || !explained) return;
825	    const s = reviewSite;
826	    s.state = "added";
827	    s.meltT = MELT_DUR;                 // the seal melts; the upgrade wakes up
828	    const anim = s.upgradeModel.userData.anim;
829	    if (anim?.type === "spire") anim.beam.visible = true;
830	    updateSystems();
831	    if (allAdded()) {
832	      // The fifth accept doesn't close the terminal — the finish line is the
833	      // next command at the prompt you're already at, like the real CLI.
834	      termMode = "report";
835	      reviewSite = null;
836	      explained = false;
837	      buffer = "";
838	      termList?.classList.add("hidden");
839	      flashTerminal("all five systems online", true);
840	      showTutorial("Every system accounted for — send the day's report: type `entire dispatch`.", 0);
841	      renderTerminal();
842	    } else {
843	      closeTerminal(false);
844	      showTutorial(`${s.sys.name} online (${addedCount()} / ${sites.length}).`, 5000);
845	    }
846	  }
847	  // The ADD TO SHIP button (terminal CTA is re-rendered, so delegate the click).
848	  termCta?.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
849	    if (!active) return;
850	    if (e.target?.id === "db-add-btn") addToShip();
851	  });
852	
853	  // ---------- the finish line: entire dispatch ----------
854	  // "Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work" — five drones just
855	  // worked; the report writes itself from their checkpoints.
856	  function sendDispatch() {
857	    reportSent = true;
858	    timerRunning = false;
859	    countdownEl?.classList.remove("is-low", "is-critical");
860	    if (termList) {
861	      termList.innerHTML =
862	        `<div class="term-list-row"><span class="tl-key tl-exp-key">DISPATCH</span>` +
863	        `<span class="tl-title">drone bay — day report</span></div>` +
864	        sites.map((s) =>
865	          `<div class="term-list-row"><span class="tl-key tl-exp-key">·</span>` +
866	          `<span class="tl-title">${s.sys.name.toLowerCase()} → ${s.sys.became} (${s.sys.ckpt.slice(0, 6)}…)</span></div>`
867	        ).join("") +
868	        `<div class="term-list-row"><span class="tl-key tl-exp-key">filed</span>` +
869	        `<span class="tl-title">from 5 checkpoints · crew: 1 human, 5 subagents</span></div>`;

> AGENT

Read the whole Level 2 (`droneBayView.js`) plus its HUD markup. Functionally it's solid — the delegate → review → accept loop works, the improvised upgrades are a great touch, the parallel-vs-serial pressure is real. The thing that jumps out is that **Level 2 is still written in the exact instruction style you just threw out of Level 1.** Everything we fixed last session, L2 still does the old way.

Here's the gap, concretely:

**1. The briefing is the "too much up front" wall — again.**
`#db-briefing` is the dense card: a story paragraph, a 4-step numbered "YOUR MISSION" list, a full controls grid, *and* a warning line — all before the player has done anything. This is precisely what you cut from L1 ("it's too much for them to read up front"). L1 now opens with 4 short pilot-voice beats in the gold banner. L2 should too.

**2. The "random words popping up" are all still here.**
L2 leans on `teachOnce()` toasts for everything important — `"The subagent's got it — you're free…"`, `"A subagent finished while you were away…"`, `"That's the story behind the checkpoint…"`. That's the mid-game noise you didn't want players reading under pressure. In L1 we moved teaching into the story-banner surface and made the rest quiet.

**3. There's no clock-off tutorial gate.**
L1 now does: briefing → **practice one record, clock off** → "PLAY LEVEL 1, clock starts." L2 drops you straight into a 150s timed run with a brand-new command (`entire checkpoint explain`) you've never typed. The first delegate→review→accept cycle is the perfect thing to rehearse with the clock off, same as L1's first record.

So the headline: **bring L2 up to the L1 teaching pattern** — short banner beats, a clock-off first-system tutorial, teach `explain` in the gold lesson surface, then go quiet.

Two smaller things worth a decision while we're here:

- **L2 actually teaches *two* new commands** — `entire checkpoint explain` (the lesson) *and* `entire dispatch` (the finish line). Your own rule was "one new command per level." `dispatch` works as a finale flourish, but it's worth deciding whether it's "a command to learn" or just "the big red button you happen to type."
- **The core insight of L2 — "delegating five in parallel beats babysitting one" — is currently taught by a toast, not by a moment.** That's the whole level. It might land harder as a felt beat (e.g., the first time you stand watching one drone and the clock visibly bleeds) than as a sentence.

> AGENT

Yeah — I think the subagents idea is genuinely one of the *truer* metaphors in the whole game, and the "they do work behind the scenes and you don't see how" instinct is exactly the right thing to be teaching. Let me be honest about where it's strong and where it's currently soft, though, because the concept is sound but the level under-delivers on it.

**Why it makes sense (keep this):**
- Drones = subagents is a clean, literal mapping, not a stretch.
- "You can only be one place; they run in parallel" is the real reason people reach for subagents.
- **"A subagent finished while you were away and its work is sealed under a checkpoint"** — that's the single most accurate beat in the level. That *is* the experience: you come back and there's work you didn't watch.
- The improvise idea — a bent dish comes back as a signal spire — is the best part. Real agents don't do exactly what you pictured; they make calls. "The transformation is what makes you need the explanation" is a great line of reasoning.

So the concept is good. The honest problem is the level doesn't make "you don't know the behind the scenes" actually *bite*. Two soft spots:

**1. You never actually *ask* for anything.** You walk up and press E — that's "turn the machine on," not "delegate a goal." Because you never said "fix the antenna," the surprise ("it built a spire instead") has no expectation to violate. The "I didn't know it'd do THAT" gut-punch needs a *that* to be measured against. Right now broken→upgrade just happens and `explain` narrates it after the fact.

**2. Understanding has no stakes.** You `explain`, then you ADD TO SHIP — but you'd add it whether you read it or not. Nothing punishes a blind accept. So `explain` reads as ceremony before a rubber-stamp Y, when the real lesson is "understand agent work *before* you accept it, because you're accountable for it."

The fix isn't to drop subagents — it's to make the behind-the-scenes *matter*:
- **Give each job a stated intent** ("the antenna's down — send someone") so the improvised result lands as a deviation you have to reckon with. The gap between what you asked and what you got is the entire reason to open `explain`.
- **Make accepting a real judgment call.** Maybe one of the five did something genuinely debatable — over-budget, scope-creeped, "technically the ship floats now." Reading the explain is how you catch it and decide. That turns `explain` from a step into the thing that saves you. (This also rhymes with your L3 design — the "occasional dead end / not every answer is clean" idea.)

So my real answer: **the subagents conceit is a keeper — it's the most honest part of the game.** What's missing is that the "behind the scenes" never costs you anything, so the level *tells* you agents surprise you instead of *making* you feel it. Want to dig into making the delegate-then-discover gap real — the "I asked for X, it did Y, now I have to decide" loop?

131	// ?view=level2 (or ?level=2) to Level 2, ?view=level3 (or ?level=3) to the

> AGENT

Good catch — and digging through the actual handoff code, I think the clunkiness is real and it's a few small things stacked, not one bug. Here's the path a player actually walks from "I beat Level 1" to "I'm playing Level 2":

1. The L1 clock has to hit **0:00** — there's no early finish. Even once you've banked your 4, you wait out the rest of the 40s.
2. At zero, the terminal pops and you have to **type `entire checkpoint list` + Enter** to see your haul.
3. Then **Enter again** ("Press Enter to investigate").
4. Then you land in L2 and get hit with the **dense `db-briefing` card**, which needs another read + another key.

That's a lot of ceremony right at the victory moment, and it's exactly where it should feel like a reward, not a checklist.

On the **Esc specifically** — I went looking and Level 1 has *no* pointer lock and no Esc handler at all, so the Esc you're pressing almost certainly belongs to **Level 2's** first-person mouse-capture (Esc releases the mouse so you can click START on the briefing). That tells me the rough seam is the *arrival* into L2, not the exit from L1. Can you confirm: is the "esc then enter" happening once you're already looking at the L2 briefing card?

Either way, here's how I'd smooth it:

- **One clean handoff beat.** Replace the type-a-command-then-double-Enter ending with a single "LEVEL 1 COMPLETE — the drone bay just woke up · press Enter" card that fades straight into L2. One key, no typing chore at the win.
- **Don't make `entire checkpoint list` a gate.** It's a nice payoff, but advancing shouldn't depend on typing it *and* then pressing Enter again. Show the haul automatically, advance on one key.
- **Land softer in L2.** Since we're already planning to redo L2's onboarding in the L1 banner style, the dense briefing card goes away — so you arrive into short beats, not a wall, and the mouse-capture/Esc dance disappears with it.

The cleanest version: L1 ends → one "next level" card → Enter → L2 opens with a calm pilot-voice beat, no Esc needed anywhere.

Want me to confirm the Esc spot with you first, or should I just sketch the single-card handoff and you react to it?

Builds clean. Here's what changed:

**The new L1 → L2 handoff:**
1. Clock hits 0:00, you passed → terminal opens asking for `entire checkpoint list` (unchanged — that's the teaching beat you wanted to keep).
2. You type it + Enter → your recovered-records haul lists out in the terminal.
3. A centered card fades in over it, in the **same title-screen style** as the tutorial/play gate:

   > **LEVEL 1 COMPLETE**
   > **START LEVEL 2**
   > Ship memory restored — the drone bay just woke up.
   > `Space` to select

4. Space / Enter / click the button → straight to Level 2. (B still drops to orbit.)

The haul list stays visible behind the card (I made the "next" mode keep the terminal open instead of closing it, unlike the tutorial/play prompts). No more tiny "Press Enter to investigate" toast, and no Esc anywhere in the L1 exit path — that Esc you were hitting was Level 2's mouse-capture, which we'll dissolve when we redo L2's onboarding.

It reuses the existing `level-mode-prompt` component, so it's one consistent visual language across all the gates now. Want to playtest it, or should I commit?

> AGENT

Only the background music exists so far — no SFX, and assets live in `public/audio/`. My recommendation: **synthesize the effects with the Web Audio API** rather than hunting down sound files. For a retro arcade shooter it's the right fit — no asset/licensing hassle, tiny footprint, instant, and it matches the CRT vibe. Easy to swap for sampled sounds later if you want richer ones.

Let me build a tasteful first pass you can actually hear and react to. I'll create a small `sfx.js` module and wire it into the L1 moments: shooting, recovering a record, hitting wreckage, the bank steps (stage/freeze/link), and the pass/fail stings — all respecting the existing mute button.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/goose-guest/Documents/work/planetfall-seed-signalkit/src/sfx.js",
  "content": "// Synthesized sound effects for the arcade levels. No audio assets — everything\n// is generated with the Web Audio API so it stays tiny and fits the retro/CRT\n// feel. One shared AudioContext, created and resumed on the first (gesture-\n// driven) play. Honors the global mute, wired in main.js to the music button.\n\nlet ctx = null;\nlet master = null;\nlet muted = false;\n\nfunction ensure() {\n  if (ctx) return ctx;\n  const AC = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext;\n  if (!AC) return null;\n  ctx = new AC();\n  master = ctx.createGain();\n  master.gain.value = 0.6;\n  master.connect(ctx.destination);\n  return ctx;\n}\nfunction resume() {\n  if (ctx && ctx.state === \"suspended\") ctx.resume();\n}\n\n// One enveloped oscillator: freq → to (optional glide) with a short AD envelope.\nfunction tone({ freq, to, type = \"sine\", dur = 0.15, vol = 0.3, attack = 0.005, delay = 0, detune = 0 }) {\n  if (!ensure() || muted) return;\n  resume();\n  const t0 = ctx.currentTime + delay;\n  const osc = ctx.createOscillator();\n  const g = ctx.createGain();\n  osc.type = type;\n  osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, t0);\n  if (to && to !== freq) osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(1, to), t0 + dur);\n  if (detune) osc.detune.value = detune;\n  g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t0);\n  g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(vol, t0 + attack);\n  g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t0 + dur);\n  osc.connect(g).connect(master);\n  osc.start(t0);\n  osc.stop(t0 + dur + 0.02);\n}\n\n// A short decaying noise burst, for impacts.\nfunction noise({ dur = 0.12, vol = 0.25, type = \"highpass\", freq = 800, delay = 0 }) {\n  if (!ensure() || muted) return;\n  resume();\n  const t0 = ctx.currentTime + delay;\n  const n = Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * dur);\n  const buf = ctx.createBuffer(1, n, ctx.sampleRate);\n  const d = buf.getChannelData(0);\n  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) d[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / n);\n  const src = ctx.createBufferSource();\n  src.buffer = buf;\n  const f = ctx.createBiquadFilter();\n  f.type = type;\n  f.frequency.value = freq;\n  const g = ctx.createGain();\n  g.gain.setValueAtTime(vol, t0);\n  g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t0 + dur);\n  src.connect(f).connect(g).connect(master);\n  src.start(t0);\n  src.stop(t0 + dur);\n}\n\nexport const sfx = {\n  setMuted(m) { muted = !!m; },\n  setVolume(v) { if (ensure()) master.gain.value = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v)); },\n  resume,\n\n  // Cannon bolt — a quick descending zap.\n  shoot() {\n    tone({ freq: 760, to: 180, type: \"sawtooth\", dur: 0.13, vol: 0.18, attack: 0.004 });\n    noise({ dur: 0.06, vol: 0.06, type: \"highpass\", freq: 1200 });\n  },\n  // Record recovered — bright two-note rise.\n  recover() {\n    tone({ freq: 640, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.1, vol: 0.22 });\n    tone({ freq: 960, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.16, vol: 0.22, delay: 0.08 });\n  },\n  // Wrong target (wreckage) — low detuned buzzer.\n  wrong() {\n    tone({ freq: 150, to: 90, type: \"square\", dur: 0.2, vol: 0.2 });\n    tone({ freq: 151, to: 88, type: \"square\", dur: 0.2, vol: 0.12, detune: 8 });\n  },\n  // git add — soft stage click.\n  stage() {\n    tone({ freq: 520, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.07, vol: 0.18 });\n  },\n  // git commit — freeze into ice (icy descending shimmer).\n  freeze() {\n    tone({ freq: 1320, to: 720, type: \"sine\", dur: 0.28, vol: 0.16 });\n    tone({ freq: 1980, to: 1080, type: \"sine\", dur: 0.28, vol: 0.08, delay: 0.02 });\n  },\n  // Checkpoint linked — little ascending sparkle chime.\n  link() {\n    tone({ freq: 880, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.1, vol: 0.2 });\n    tone({ freq: 1175, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.1, vol: 0.18, delay: 0.07 });\n    tone({ freq: 1568, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.18, vol: 0.18, delay: 0.14 });\n  },\n  // Run passed — triumphant rise.\n  pass() {\n    [523, 659, 784, 1047].forEach((f, i) =>\n      tone({ freq: f, type: \"triangle\", dur: 0.22, vol: 0.2, delay: i * 0.1 }));\n  },\n  // Run failed — descending tones.\n  fail() {\n    [392, 311, 233].forEach((f, i) =>\n      tone({ freq: f, type: \"sawtooth\", dur: 0.26, vol: 0.16, delay: i * 0.13 }));\n  },\n  // Unrecognized command — quiet low double blip.\n  deny() {\n    tone({ freq: 200, type: \"square\", dur: 0.06, vol: 0.12 });\n    tone({ freq: 160, type: \"square\", dur: 0.08, vol: 0.12, delay: 0.07 });\n  },\n};\n"
}

{

  "new_string": "  const tryPlayMusic = () => {\n    if (userPausedMusic) return;\n    bgm.play().then(updateAudioUi).catch(updateAudioUi);\n  };\n\n  // Sidechain ducking: dip the music instantly on a hit, then ramp it back to\n  // the player's set volume so the SFX punch through a momentary hole.\n  let duckRAF = null;\n  const duckMusic = (depth = 0.5, ms = 350) => {\n    if (bgm.muted) return;\n    const base = Number(audioVolume.value);\n    const floor = Math.max(0, base * depth);\n    bgm.volume = floor;\n    const start = performance.now();\n    cancelAnimationFrame(duckRAF);\n    const step = (now) => {\n      const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / ms);\n      bgm.volume = floor + (base - floor) * t;\n      if (t < 1) duckRAF = requestAnimationFrame(step);\n    };\n    duckRAF = requestAnimationFrame(step);\n  };\n  sfx.setDucker(duckMusic);"
}

Builds clean. Ducking is in — give it a listen. Here's how it's tuned:

| Event | Music dips to | Ramp back |
|---|---|---|
| Shoot | 80% (barely) | 130 ms |
| Good hit | 40% | 380 ms |
| Bad hit | 35% | 420 ms |

The dip is **instant**, then the music swells back to your set volume over the ramp — that's what makes the hit "pop" out of a hole rather than just stacking on top. It respects mute, and it ramps back to whatever the volume slider is at (so it won't fight your volume setting).

A couple of things to feel out as you play:
- **Shoot ducking** is deliberately tiny (80%/130ms) because you fire constantly — anything deeper makes the music pump on rapid fire. If even that feels like it's "breathing," I'll drop the shoot duck entirely and only duck the hits.
- If the hit dip feels too **deep** (music drops out too much) or too **slow** to recover, I can nudge the depth/ms.

> AGENT

Here's the lay of the land before I give you my take:

- The **SOUND** options panel (`#ts-sound`) today has just two rows: a **MUSIC** on/off toggle and a music **VOLUME** slider (with %, keyboard arrows, and mouse drag).
- `sfx.js` already exposes `setVolume()` (it scales the SFX master gain), so the plumbing for an SFX slider is basically already there — it'd just need a row in the panel and a bit of wiring.
- One thing to note: the music volume **isn't persisted** (only the TV effect is saved to `localStorage`). So to match the existing pattern, an SFX setting wouldn't persist either unless we add it for both.

**My recommendation: yes, add a single SFX volume slider** that mirrors the music one. In a panel literally labeled SOUND, players expect separate music/SFX control, and "drag to 0" already covers the "turn it off" case — so one slider does the whole job without adding clutter. It's the natural symmetric addition, not feature creep.

That said, it's a real call given your simplicity bar, so let me check which way you want it:
